claim: Finstad and Johnson debated on Oct 8 on two southern Minnesota TV stations (MPR News)

Finstad defended Trump's tariffs and cited $50 billion in rural health care funding; Johnson called tariffs a tax, said he would vote to end them and said the administration cut $137 billion from rural health care through Medicaid (MPR News; each figure is the candidate's claim)
More than $2.5 million of outside spending has flowed into MN-01, most of it opposing Finstad (MPR News, citing FEC data)
A group tied to House Majority Whip Tom Emmer deployed $600,000 in ads critical of Johnson that week (MPR News)
Outside spending in this district has outpaced the statewide Senate race (MPR News)

Johnson, a math teacher and first-time candidate, has outspent Finstad by more than $500,000 and GOP PACs recently added about $400,000 (FOX 9; no source given; the $600,000 and $400,000 Republican-side figures are not reconciled)
Political scientist Larry Jacobs of the University of Minnesota links the district's competitiveness to farm affordability pressure he ties to tariffs and the Iran war (FOX 9)
